exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 The Poetry Contest
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Teacher
transcript.text: Our city is holding a poetry contest. Would any of you like to enter?

transcript.speaker: Nora
transcript.text: I'd love to, but when is the deadline?

transcript.speaker: Teacher
transcript.text: You must send in your poem by the end of next week.

transcript.speaker: Nora
transcript.text: Then I still need a few days to polish my writing.

transcript.speaker: Pitt
transcript.text: I don't think I'll enter. My poems are far too simple.

transcript.speaker: Teacher
transcript.text: Don't worry, Pitt. Even an amateur can win if the feeling is true.

transcript.speaker: George
transcript.text: I'm going to write a poem about my grandmother and the songs she taught me.

transcript.speaker: Teacher
transcript.text: That's a wonderful idea. Give it your best shot!

exercises.translation_cn: 老师说城里要办诗歌比赛,问谁想参加;诺拉想参加,问截止日期;老师说下周末前交诗;诺拉说还需几天润色;皮特觉得自己的诗太简单,不想参加;老师鼓励说即便业余爱好者只要感情真挚也能获奖;乔治打算写一首关于祖母和她教的歌的诗;老师称赞并鼓励他全力以赴。

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 What Is a Haiku
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: A haiku is a short form of poetry that comes from Japan.
It is made up of just seventeen syllables in three lines.
The three lines hold five, seven and five syllables respectively.
With so few words, a haiku can still paint a clear picture.
Many haiku describe a single quiet moment in nature.
exercises.translation_cn: 俳句是源自日本的一种短诗;仅由三行十七个音节组成;三行依次为五、七、五个音节;尽管词很少,俳句仍能描绘清晰的画面;许多俳句描写自然中安静的一瞬。

questions.stem: Where does the haiku come from?
How many syllables does a haiku have?
How are the syllables arranged?
What can a haiku do with very few words?
What do many haiku describe?

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Choosing a Poem
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: I have to read a poem aloud tomorrow, but I can't decide which one.

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: What about 'Dream' by Langston Hughes? It's very short.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: I like that one. It tells us to hold fast to our dreams.

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: And its lines rhyme, so it sounds lovely when you read it aloud.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: True. But maybe I should choose a Tang poem instead.

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: A Tang poem is beautiful too, but it may be harder to recite.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: You're right. I'll go with 'Dream'. It feels closer to my heart.

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: Good choice. Just read it slowly and with feeling.

exercises.translation_cn: 米娅明天要朗诵一首诗却拿不定主意;利奥建议读休斯的《梦想》,很短;米娅喜欢,说它教人坚守梦想;利奥说它押韵,朗读起来好听;米娅又想读唐诗;利奥说唐诗也美,但可能更难吟诵;米娅决定选《梦想》,觉得更贴近内心;利奥让她慢慢地、带着感情读。

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 How to Read a Poem Aloud
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Poetry should always be read aloud, for that is when you hear its music.
When you read aloud, start slowly and find the rhythm of the words.
Think about how the poem makes you feel before you begin.
Then read it with that emotion, pouring out your feelings.
Read it more than once, because each reading brings something new.
exercises.translation_cn: 诗歌应当大声朗读,因为那时你能听到它的音乐;朗读时要慢慢开始,找到词语的节奏;开始前想想这首诗带给你的感受;然后带着那份情感朗读,倾诉你的感情;多读几遍,因为每一遍都会带来新的东西。

options: How the poem makes you feel.

questions.stem: How should you read the poem?
options: With emotion, pouring out your feelings.

options: Because it is required by law.

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Writing Our Own Poem
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I want to write my own poem, but I don't know how to start.

transcript.speaker: Ann
transcript.text: Begin with a theme. Ask what message you want to give the reader.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: All right. I think I'll write about the wind on the hill.

transcript.speaker: Ann
transcript.text: Good. Now make a list of words that match that theme.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Like 'fly', 'kite', 'string' and 'sky'. Some of them even rhyme.

transcript.speaker: Ann
transcript.text: Perfect. Then check how well your words paint a picture in your head.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: And after that I read it aloud to hear how it sounds, right?

transcript.speaker: Ann
transcript.text: Exactly. Finally, give it a title, and your poem is ready.

exercises.translation_cn: 汤姆想写自己的诗却不知如何开始;安建议从主题入手,先想清楚要传达什么信息;汤姆决定写山上的风;安让他列出与主题相关的词;汤姆想到 fly、kite、string、sky,有些还押韵;安让他检查这些词能否在脑海中描绘画面;汤姆问之后是不是要朗读听听效果;安说没错,最后取个标题,诗就完成了。

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 The Beauty of Poems
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Poems paint pictures with words, using images and comparisons.
Their sounds, rhythm and rhymes give them a musical quality.
A short poem can carry a deep feeling in only a few lines.
Some poems make us happy, while others fill us with quiet sorrow.
Whatever the feeling, a good poem stays in the mind for a long time.
exercises.translation_cn: 诗歌用文字描绘画面,运用意象和比喻;它们的声音、节奏和押韵赋予其音乐般的特质;一首短诗只用寥寥数行便能承载深沉的情感;有的诗让我们快乐,有的让我们充满淡淡的忧伤;无论是何种情感,一首好诗都会长久地留在心间。

questions.stem: How do poems paint pictures?
What gives poems a musical quality?
What can a short poem carry?
options: A deep feeling in a few lines.
